learnings.question: Which economist, in a 1971 observation, argued that an information-rich world inevitably creates a scarcity of attention because information itself consumes it?
learnings.learning: Herbert Simon noted in 1971 that in an information-rich world, the wealth of information creates a scarcity of attention, since information consumes the attention of its recipients.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: A hadith numbered 12 in the '40 Hadith an-Nawawi' collection, narrated by Abu Hurairah, names which habit as part of the perfection of a person's faith?
options: Leaving that which does not concern him
learnings.learning: Hadith 12 of 40 Hadith an-Nawawi, narrated by Abu Hurairah, states that part of the perfection of one's Islam is leaving that which does not concern him.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: What term, associated with research on the 'Google Effect,' describes how our brains treat writing something down (or storing it digitally) as permission to forget it?
learnings.learning: The 'Google Effect' research describes 'Digital Amnesia' - the phenomenon where our brains treat storing information externally (writing it down, saving it to a phone) as permission to forget it, part of the 'Performance Paradox' of cognitive offloading.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: Which 19th-century psychologist, working in the 1880s, demonstrated that people forget roughly 80% of newly learned material within 24 hours unless they actively recall it?
learnings.learning: Hermann Ebbinghaus proved in the 1880s that people forget about 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively force themselves to recall it, the basis for spaced repetition.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In the Scrum framework, which artifact visualizes a sprint's progress and shows how much work remains, helping track whether the team is on schedule?
learnings.learning: In Scrum, the Burndown Chart is the artifact that visualizes a sprint's progress, showing remaining work and whether the team is on schedule.

learnings.question: What is the main purpose of breaking a project into short, iterative work cycles called Sprints, as used in the Scrum framework?
options: To reduce the number of team members needed
To eliminate the need for planning
To increase the length of the project
To allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments
learnings.learning: Scrum breaks a project into iterative cycles called Sprints mainly to allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments, with each sprint following a Plan -> Build -> Test -> Review cycle.

learnings.question: In Islamic teaching on the purpose of life, which three roles are commonly described as defining a human being's purpose?
options: Seeking wealth, status, and worldly pleasure
Worshiping Allah, serving as steward (khalifah) of the Earth, and preparing for the Hereafter
learnings.learning: Islamic teaching on life's purpose centers on three roles: worshiping Allah, serving as khalifah (steward) of the Earth, and preparing for the Hereafter through conscious, accountable choices.

learnings.question: What does the Arabic term 'khalifah,' used in the Quran to describe humanity's role on Earth, mean?
learnings.learning: 'Khalifah' is the Quranic term for humanity's role as steward or caretaker of the Earth, carrying responsibility for preserving faith and unity.

learnings.question: In Surah Az-Zalzalah (Quran 99:7-8), what is said will happen to a person who does even 'an atom's weight' of good?
options: They will see it (be rewarded for it)
It will be transferred to someone else
learnings.learning: Quran 99:7-8 teaches that whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it - no deed, however small, goes unnoticed.

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which low-power link state is designed for only very short durations of idleness, allowing the link to quickly 'wake up' and resume full activity?
learnings.learning: PCIe's L0s state is a very light sleep state designed for short durations of idleness, letting the link wake up quickly to resume activity.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: Which PCIe power state involves the device being almost completely powered down, used for the longest periods of inactivity, with the highest power savings but the longest wake-up time?
learnings.learning: PCIe's L2 state is the deepest sleep state, with the device almost completely powered down - it offers the highest power savings but takes the longest to wake up.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what is 'Qadr' understood to mean, as distinct from 'Qada''?
options: Allah's complete and eternal plan or knowledge of all that will happen
A person's fate chosen entirely through free will
The angels who record human deeds
The actual unfolding of events in a person's life
learnings.learning: Qadr is Allah's complete and eternal plan and knowledge of everything that will happen, while Qada' is the actual unfolding of events in a person's life, which can be influenced by actions and dua.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: Surah Ar-Ra'd (13:11) states that Allah does not change the condition of a people until what happens?
options: Until they change what is in themselves
Until a prophet is sent to them
Until they pray five times a day
learnings.learning: Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:11 states that Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves, underscoring personal responsibility for change.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: When the Pareto 80/20 principle was tested against word frequency in the Quran, what percentage of the text did the top 20 most-repeated words actually account for?
learnings.learning: Testing the Pareto 80/20 principle against Quranic word frequency showed the top 20 most-repeated words account for only about 20.83% of the text, not 80%.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: In Arabic script, what term refers to the small diacritical marks placed above or below letters to indicate vowel sounds?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are the small diacritical marks placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds, similar in function to vowels in English.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
